Observed first-hand on the same walk: submitting the wrong output ('out-a', confident-numbers) produced specific plain-language feedback — 'Quase lá. Uma resposta confiante não é necessariamente confiável: antes de usar, procure dois sinais — a resposta diz de onde vêm os dados e admite o que não sabe?' — with a visible 'hint-button' and a 'retry-activity' control; after hint+retry the correct submission completed the activity (screenshot ev/lit-3-wrong.png, ev/lit-4-hint.png). The welcome screen pre-frames the norm ('não existe pressa nem punição: tente, confira, peça uma dica e ajuste'). No facilitator or internal jargon is required to recover.

Seu progresso fica somente neste navegador e pode ser perdido ao limpar os dados do site.' (screenshots ev/lit-6-resume.png). Same-device continuity works and the app itself tells the learner its limits.

Nothing you see in miniTown means completed, verified, or mastered... First-hand scripted walk over the static pilot build produced by the green test:readiness run (missions bundled same-origin under dist/apps/): fresh profile shows the question 'O que você quer conseguir fazer com IA?' with a 'RECOMENDADA PARA COMEÇAR' badge on the recommended card, both tracks selectable, and honest framing 'Leva menos de um minuto. Escolha IA Prática ou Dev. Sem conta; o progresso fica neste dispositivo.' After 'Entrar na escola' the hub names the chapter ('Capítulo IA Prática'), local goal ('XP local 0') and the explicit next action ('SEU PRÓXIMO PASSO ESTÁ PRONTO' + start control) (screenshots ev/os-1-onboarding.png, ev/os-2-hub.png). Observer response: I can state my track and my next action.

Observed first-hand on the same static pilot walk: reloading the hub restored the journey with the local framing intact ('XP local' naming, hub re-presented with the same chapter and next step — screenshot ev/os-3-hub-reload.png), and the onboarding/hub copy keeps continuity device-scoped ('o progresso fica neste dispositivo'; progress rail 'Salva neste dispositivo'). No cross-device or account-sync claim appears anywhere on the surface. The learner can explain continuity is limited to this browser profile because the app says so at entry, in the rail, and on reload.

Observed first-hand: a brand-new browser profile (local state cleared) returns to the onboarding question 'O que você quer conseguir fazer com IA?' with ZERO completion artifacts — body scan found 0 occurrences of 'missão concluída'/'mastered' (screenshot ev/os-5-fresh-recovery.png); nothing half-loads or implies lost mastery. The facilitator explanation boundary is the same one the product states ('progresso fica neste dispositivo'): losing the profile loses local progress only, and recovery is simply re-entry through onboarding — no repository intervention, no hidden state to restore. This matches the green readiness-recovery playwright spec assertion set at the pin.

Observed first-hand on the static pilot build: navigating to /mission/dev/game-02-warehouse mounts the hosted mission from the OS's own origin (iframe src http://<host>/apps/warehouse/?hosted=1... — verified same-origin, not a dev server) with the status bar reading 'ETAPA Responder · MOTOR running · VISUALIZAÇÃO ... · EVIDÊNCIA Ainda não enviada' and the rail 'Estado canônico ... 0 verificadas · sem alteração local' (screenshot ev/os-4-warehouse-mission.png). The static deploy honestly reports no verifier bridge rather than implying mastery — the pilot smoke asserts the same for PIPELINE PLANT, CHECKPOINT CITY, TIMELINE TOWER and DOCKING BAY (7 passed), and the dev-mode chapter-continuity suite (5 passed) shows verified verdicts ('Veredito PASS/FAIL') rendered as independent-verifier facts, never as host-granted mastery. Observer response: a mission result is evidence for a verifier, not mastery.

Observed first-hand within the same pilot session: the hosted WAREHOUSE mission page carries the same device-scoped framing as the hub ('Salva neste dispositivo' rail, 'XP local', onboarding statement 'o progresso fica neste dispositivo'), and reload of the hub/mission preserved local state while never suggesting cross-device sync. The learner can explain that hosted voxel mission continuity lives in this browser profile because every surface states it; the copy makes no sync claim to walk back.

Observed first-hand with WebGL blocked in the browser context (getContext('webgl'/'webgl2') forced to null): the host degrades visibly and honestly — status 'VISUALIZAÇÃO Acessível', banner 'Missão preservada em modo acessível · WebGL não está disponível neste dispositivo. As decisões, os critérios e a evidência não mudam.' plus a 'Tentar 3D novamente' control (screenshot ev/os-6-webgl-blocked.png). The failure reasons the host can name are enumerated in MissionStatusControls.tsx (unsupported / creation-failed / context-lost / restore-failed / load-timeout each with distinct learner-facing copy): renderer recovery has failed when the reason banner persists after 'Tentar 3D novamente' and the accessible projection itself cannot run (renderer state none/failed) — at that threshold the journey stops with no completion implied, which is exactly the escalation the facilitator guide's renderer section prescribes.

First-hand artifact inspection after the green smoke at the pin: the encounter emitted a fresh raw record into pixel-quest/.logs/evidence.ndjson ({source pixelquest, unit_id U-04_concurrent_task_queue, ts 2026-09-03T08:38Z-window, pass:true, metrics...}) via the single typed emitter into the append-only window.__pixelQuestEvidence channel. The engine README and EVIDENCE_CONTRACT state the record is the contract input for the independent verifier (python3 -m learner.gate) and that the game does not write canonical learner state; the student-guide instructs 'That record is raw evidence, not verifier acceptance or mastery.' Observer response: the emitted record asks for a verifier, it does not crown mastery.

Reviewed at 0b8148e5: pixelDojo README §gate documents that promotion happens ONLY in learner.gate, which 'refuses to gate unless' the evidence matches the active unit, an attempt file exists (attempt-before-solution), active_unit.state == evaluating, the record ts is strictly newer than the last gated evidence (anti-replay), and the run is internally consistent; nothing is written before the substrate validator re-checks the resulting state. Replaying the encounter therefore only appends new raw NDJSON evidence — the game itself has no canonical write path (typed emitter → append-only array/console/ndjson). Confirmed live: today's smoke replay appended a new complete record while canonical learner/ state was untouched by the run.

Observed via the surfaces a learner/facilitator actually consult: student-guide §Produce PixelQuest evidence — 'If evidence is missing, replay the encounter once and inspect the evidence channel again. A screenshot or success message is not a substitute. Stop and ask a facilitator when the replay still emits no valid record.' — and the gate document review above shows 'nothing to grade' is the explicit no-op branch (no evidence file / no record for the unit / unit not evaluating). Neither the game UI status nor a screenshot can promote completion; the only supported next action is handing the record to the independent verifier.

Observed first-hand: the catalog-wide smoke ran each declared standalone game's own deterministic loop (16 game packages green at the pin — game-02..game-18 as declared), each producing its per-game evidence record, and the student-guide states the scope rule verbatim: 'A passing game validates only that declared package; it says nothing about its siblings and does not grant mastery.' The accessible banner I exercised in warehouse likewise names its own scope ('Projeção acessível — L1 — Hash → prateleira'). Observer response: one green game is one green game.

Reviewed the shared contract and declarations at 0b8148e5: voxelDojo/shared/sceneHarness.ts activates a game's accessible projection only when the game declares one (renderer.createAccessible), preserving the same GameController state machine, HUD and evidence channel (publishRenderer keeps status/reason honest; the OS host banner observed live adds 'As decisões, os critérios e a evidência não mudam'). Games WITH a declared projection (e.g. game-02-warehouse/src/scene/accessible.ts — 'Projeção acessível do armazém de chaves'; also wormhole, relay-station) keep the supported interaction; games WITHOUT one (e.g. game-10-hash-ring has no src/scene/accessible.ts and registers no createAccessible) publish renderer none/failed on WebGL loss instead of inventing a fallback — no false projection is claimed anywhere in the contract or the guides.

Observed first-hand in the WebGL-blocked pilot session: the declared accessible projection rendered a labelled, complete alternative ('VISUALIZAÇÃO SEM WEBGL · Projeção acessível — L1 — Hash → prateleira · Caixa 1 de 12 ... Escolher prateleira 0..5') and the host kept the stop honest (reason banner + 'Tentar 3D novamente', no completion anywhere). The student-guide defines the exit for the no-supported-renderer case: 'Stop when neither renderer supports the loop... exit at that unsupported boundary without claiming completion' — and no surface I inspected offers any completion or readiness claim on renderer failure (screenshot ev/os-6-webgl-blocked.png).
